units.text: A room of leather and dust.
An oak desk, a reel-to-reel recorder, a glass of sherry with a lipstick ring.
The French windows are shut, the curtains drawn.
AGATHA PENHALLOW, 60s, silver hair, pearls, black gloves, sits upright at the desk with her hands folded.
Tape one. Tuesday the fourteenth. I begin this record of my own free will and in sound mind.
units.name: AGATHA

units.text: Tuesday the fourteenth. I begin this record of my own free will and in sound mind.
units.name: AGATHA

units.text: She smiles faintly and stops it again.
Nobody ever believes a woman in pearls.
units.name: AGATHA

units.text: Quite right. Let me begin properly.
units.name: AGATHA

units.text: My name is Agatha Penhallow. On the night of the fourteenth, my husband Lionel was found dead in this room. The coroner said his heart. The vicar said providence. The maid said nothing at all, which is why I trusted her.
units.name: AGATHA

units.text: I should say first that I did not like Lionel. I should say second that I did not kill him. And I should say third, since these things are the sort that must be said third, that I know who did.
units.name: AGATHA

units.text: It was the sherry. Lionel's sherry, from the decanter on that shelf. He never drank mine. He thought I would poison him. Quite the joke, in the end.
units.name: AGATHA

units.text: Someone who knew his habits, his decanter, and his hour. Someone who stood in this room while he drank and did not call for help. Someone with a key to the cellar and a reason to forget it.
units.name: AGATHA

units.text: She lifts the glass, turns it in the firelight.

I tell you this, whoever you are, listening to this tape, because I have no one else to tell. The police have lost interest. The family has lost heart. And I have, I regret to say, lost my husband's will.
units.name: AGATHA

units.text: A clock in the hall strikes twelve.
Agatha, if you are hearing this, it is because I have already done it. Lionel did not drink the sherry. You did.
units.name: AGATHA
paren: recorded, in a different, older voice

units.text: Her gloved hand finds the edge of the desk.
I have been recording you for twenty years, my dear. Every night after supper. You never noticed the machine under the floorboard.
units.name: AGATHA

units.text: You will want to know where it is. Look under the third book on the second shelf. It is not a book.
units.name: AGATHA

units.text: Inside, a second reel, labeled in Lionel's tight script: AGATHA, THE TRUTH.
Oh, Lionel. You clever, clever man.
units.name: AGATHA

units.text: She carries the reel back to the desk and threads it onto the spindle.
Lionel, you have a terrible habit of listening at keyholes.
units.name: AGATHA
paren: recorded, her own voice again, younger, laughing

units.text: Tape one, take two. Let us begin again.
units.name: AGATHA

units.text: She looks at the glass of sherry, the lipstick ring, the dying fire.
Then, very slowly, she lifts the glass to her lips and drinks.
